title: Single-cell and WGCNA uncover a prognostic model in colorectal cancer
author: Di, Zhou, et al.
materials: The human CRC cell lines SW480 and SW620 were purchased from the ATCC Cell Bank of the United States. SW480 and SW620 cells were grown in Leibovitz’s L-15 medium (Sigma, Beijing, China) supplemented with 10% foetal bovine serum (FBS) (Gibco, Grand Island, NY, USA), 2 mmol/l glutamine, 100 U/ml penicillin, and 100 μg/ml streptomycin (Thermo Scientific, Waltham, MA, USA) in a 37 °C incubator without CO2.

Cells were transfected with interfering expression or overexpression plasmids using Lipofectamine 2000 (12,566,014, Invitrogen, Shanghai, China) following the manufacturer’s protocols. To generate the lentivirus, 293FT cells were cotransfected with psPAX2, pMD2G, pLKO.1-MPZ-GFP, pLKO.1-SCARA3-GFP, pLKO.1-MPP2-GFP or pLKO.1-PBXIP1-GFP to interfere with expression. 293FT cells were cotransfected with pLVX-MPZ-IRES-Neo-3xFlag, pLVX-SCARA3-IRES-Neo-3xFlag, pLVX-MPP2-IRES-Neo-3xFlag or pLVX-PBXIP1-IRES-Neo-3xFlag for overexpression. Forty-eight hours after transfection, the lentiviral supernatants were collected and filtered through a 0.45-μm filter. The lentiviruses were added to medium containing 8 µg/ml polybrene (Sigma, St. Louis, MO, USA) and transduced into CRC cells according to the manufacturer’s instructions. Stable cells were selected for at least 1 week using PURO (P8230-25, Solarbio, Beijing, China) or G418 (10,131,035, Invitrogen, Shanghai, China).

Furthermore, we examined the expression profiles of previously unreported model genes (MPZ, SCARA3, MPP2 and PBXIP1) in clinical samples from CRC patients by qPCR (Fig. 9A-D) and IHC (Fig. 9E-H) analysis and found that the expression levels of MPZ, SCARA3, MPP2 and PBXIP1 were high in CRC tissues.Fig. 9The expression of the unreported model genes. The results of A-D qPCR and E–H IHC analysis showed that the expression of MPZ, SCARA3, MPP2 and PBXIP1 was high in CRC tissues

steps.title: Download public transcriptome datasets
steps.instruction: Download CRC single‑cell RNA‑seq data (GSE161277) and bulk RNA‑seq data from TCGA and GSE17537.

steps.title: Cluster scRNA‑seq cells
steps.instruction: In the scRNA‑seq matrix, run Seurat functions FindNeighbors and FindClusters to obtain cell clusters.

steps.title: Estimate cluster abundance in bulk RNA‑seq
steps.instruction: Apply CIBERSORTx (R version) to the bulk RNA‑seq expression matrix (log2(TPM + 1) normalized) to obtain the relative abundance of each scRNA‑seq cluster.

steps.title: WGCNA network construction
steps.instruction: Using the R package “WGCNA”, construct a weighted gene co‑expression network from TCGA‑CRC expression profiles (431 tumour and 41 normal samples).

substeps.instruction: Define the similarity matrix for all gene pairs.
Select soft‑threshold power β = 12 (optimal soft threshold previously identified as 5) and convert the similarity matrix to an adjacency matrix.
Transform the adjacency matrix into a topological overlap matrix (TOM).
Perform hierarchical clustering of genes based on 1‑TOM (dissTOM) to build a dendrogram.
Apply the dynamic tree‑cut method to detect modules.
Calculate module eigengenes (MEs) for each module.
Compute Pearson correlations between MEs; define average distance as 1 – Pearson correlation.
Cluster MEs using average‑linkage hierarchical clustering with minimum module size set to 100 genes.
Merge modules with high similarity (height = 0.25, deepSplit = 3, minModuleSize = 100).
Result: 12 modules; the red module contains 615 genes.

steps.title: Functional enrichment of red module
steps.instruction: Run GO and KEGG enrichment on the red module using the R package “WebGestaltR”.

substeps.instruction: GO‑Biological Process: 237 terms (FDR < 0.05), report top 10.
GO‑Cellular Component: 122 terms (FDR < 0.05), report top 10.
GO‑Molecular Function: 59 terms (FDR < 0.05), report top 10.
KEGG pathways: 28 pathways (FDR < 0.05), report top 10.

steps.title: Monocle2 pseudotime analysis
steps.instruction: Use Monocle2 to order cells along a developmental trajectory.

substeps.instruction: Calculate pseudotime for each cell and scale values from 0 to 1.
Identify hub genes in each cluster with differentialGeneTest.
Reduce dimensionality with reduceDimension (max_components = 2) using the DDRTree method.
Sort cells with orderCells to assign final pseudotime values.

steps.title: Cell‑cell communication analysis
steps.instruction: Apply the R package CellChat (referred to as CellCharts) to infer ligand‑receptor interactions among the 20 clusters.

substeps.instruction: Identify high‑intensity interactions such as HLA‑C ↔ CD8A (C14 → C1), APP ↔ CD74 (C14 → C2, C7, C12, C19), and MDK ↔ SDC2 (C13/C16 → C14).

steps.title: Predict cluster abundances in TCGA and survival analysis
steps.instruction: Run CIBERSORT on TCGA‑CRC to quantify the 20 clusters; note that clusters C1, C2, C4, C5, C15, C16, C19 are high and C7, C10, C11, C13, C14, C17 are low in tumour tissue. Perform Kaplan‑Meier analysis showing high C4, C11, C13 and low C5, C14 associate with better survival; C14 correlates with prognosis.

steps.title: GSVA and risk‑score correlation
steps.instruction: Perform ssGSEA with the “GSVA” R package on all samples, compute correlation of each pathway score with the risk score, and retain pathways with |correlation| > 0.4.

substeps.instruction: Identify 8 pathways negatively and 32 pathways positively correlated with risk score.
Cluster enrichment scores of 40 KEGG pathways; note that RENAL_CELL_CARCINOMA increases with risk score.

steps.title: Mutation analysis and TMB calculation
steps.instruction: Process TCGA mutation data with Mutect2, calculate tumour mutation burden (TMB), and compare between molecular subtypes (no significant difference).

substeps.instruction: Count mutant genes per sample (no difference).
Select genes with mutation frequency >3 (12 489 genes).
Apply chi‑square test (p < 0.05) to identify high‑frequency mutated genes; retain 464 genes.

steps.title: Culture CRC cell lines
steps.instruction: Thaw and maintain human colorectal cancer cell lines SW480 and SW620 (ATCC) in Leibovitz’s L‑15 medium (Sigma, Beijing) supplemented with 10 % fetal bovine serum (Gibco), 2 mmol L⁻¹ glutamine, 100 U mL⁻¹ penicillin, and 100 µg mL⁻¹ streptomycin (Thermo Scientific) at 37 °C in a CO₂‑free incubator.

steps.title: Lentiviral vector preparation and transduction
steps.instruction: Generate lentiviruses for knock‑down or over‑expression of MPZ, SCARA3, MPP2, and PBXIP1 and transduce CRC cells.

substeps.instruction: Plasmids for knock‑down: pLKO.1‑NC‑GFP, pLKO.1‑MPZ‑GFP, pLKO.1‑SCARA3‑GFP, pLKO.1‑MPP2‑GFP, pLKO.1‑PBXIP1‑GFP.
Plasmids for over‑expression: pLVX‑IRES‑Neo‑3xFlag (empty), pLVX‑MPZ‑IRES‑Neo‑3xFlag, pLVX‑SCARA3‑IRES‑Neo‑3xFlag, pLVX‑MPP2‑IRES‑Neo‑3xFlag, pLVX‑PBXIP1‑IRES‑Neo‑3xFlag.
Packaging plasmids: psPAX2 and pMD2.G.

Transfect 293FT cells with the appropriate combination of packaging plasmids and expression vector using Lipofectamine 2000 (catalog 12,566,014, Invitrogen, Shanghai) following the manufacturer’s protocol.
Incubate transfected 293FT cells for 48 h, then collect supernatant and filter through a 0.45‑µm filter.
Add filtered lentiviral supernatant to target CRC cells in medium containing 8 µg mL⁻¹ polybrene (Sigma).
Select stably transduced cells for ≥1 week with puromycin (catalog P8230‑25, Solarbio, Beijing) or G418 (catalog 10,131,035, Invitrogen, Shanghai).

steps.title: Total RNA extraction and qRT‑PCR
steps.instruction: Isolate RNA and quantify gene expression of MPZ, SCARA3, MPP2, PBXIP1 and GAPDH by SYBR‑based qRT‑PCR.

substeps.instruction: Extract total RNA using RNA‑easy Isolation Reagent (No. RC112‑01, Vazyme).
Synthesize first‑strand cDNA with HiScript III 1st Strand cDNA Synthesis Kit (No. R312‑01, Vazyme).
Perform qPCR with ChamQ™ Universal SYBR® qPCR Master Mix (No. Q712‑02, Vazyme) according to the manufacturer’s instructions.
Use the following primer sequences (5'‑3'):
‑ MPZ: Forward CTATCCTGGCTGTGCTGCTCTT, Reverse ACTCACTGGACCAGAAGGAGCA;
‑ SCARA3: Forward CTCCGAAGACATCTCCTTGACC, Reverse CCAGCTTCATGGCAGAAAGAGC;
‑ MPP2: Forward GGCACACGTATTGACTCCATCC, Reverse GCCTCGATGAACACCACGTAAG;
‑ PBXIP1: Forward ACGCTCTTCCAGACTGAAAGCCACTGC, Reverse TCCCTGGACTACTGTGTCTCCT;
‑ GAPDH (internal control): Forward GTCTCCTCTGACTTCAACAGCG, Reverse ACCACCCTGTTGCTGTAGCCA.

steps.title: Colony formation assay and orthotopic tumour model
steps.instruction: Assess the functional impact of MPZ, SCARA3, MPP2 and PBXIP1 by performing a colony formation assay in vitro and establishing an orthotopic colorectal tumour model in vivo as described in the study.

steps.title: Statistical analysis
steps.instruction: Analyze all experimental data using R software version 3.5.3 and GraphPad Prism version 8.01. Apply Student’s t‑test for two‑group comparisons; consider p < 0.05 statistically significant.
